# SvelteKit 3 migration tasks

Some migrations are uncommon, context-dependent, or disproportionately
difficult to automate safely. This document lists them.

The findings are intentionally broad and may include files that do not
require changes.

AI agents can work through the migration tasks below one at a time:

1. Read the linked documentation or pull request before changing code.
2. Inspect every listed file and its surrounding context.
3. Ignore a finding when the file is not actually affected.
4. Make the smallest necessary change. Do not perform unrelated
   refactors or introduce unnecessary abstractions.
5. Ask the user when application intent cannot be inferred.
6. Run the project's appropriate checks after editing.

Also search the project for `@migration-task` comments. They may
describe additional manual migration work that must be resolved.

## Migration tasks

### Copy `page.url` before mutating it

`page.url` and its search parameters are readonly in SvelteKit 3.

#### What to do

Create a mutable copy with `new URL(page.url.href)`, mutate that copy,
and use it for navigation or serialization. Leave readonly accesses
unchanged.

#### References

- [Migrating to SvelteKit v3](https://next.svelte.dev/docs/kit/migrating-to-sveltekit-3#$app-state-page.url-is-now-readonly)

#### Files to review

- [ ] `src/lib/components/nav.svelte`

### Review `goto` destinations

`goto(...)` now rejects destinations that do not resolve to an
application route.

#### What to do

Confirm each destination is an internal route. Use
`window.location.href` for external browser navigation, and handle
rejected dynamic destinations where they can fail to resolve.

#### References

- [Migrating to SvelteKit v3](https://next.svelte.dev/docs/kit/migrating-to-sveltekit-3#$app-navigation-goto-rejects-for-URLs-that-don't-resolve-to-a-route)

#### Files to review

- [ ] `src/lib/components/command-palette.svelte`

### Adjust error(...) usage

Signature of `error(...)` from `@sveltejs/kit` has changed.

#### What to do

Replace `error(status, { message, ... })` with
`error(status, message, { ... })`.

#### References

- [Migrating to SvelteKit v3](<https://next.svelte.dev/docs/kit/migrating-to-sveltekit-3#Error-handling-error()-arguments-changed>)

#### Files to review

- [ ] `src/routes/newsletter/[slug]/+page.ts`
- [ ] `src/routes/posts/[slug]/+page.ts`

### Replace `invalidateAll` with `refreshAll`

`invalidateAll` is deprecated in favor of `refreshAll`

#### What to do

Replace `invalidateAll()` with `refreshAll()`. Note that
`refreshAll()` will keep `page.state` intact. Check if that has
unwanted impact on the application; if yes point this out in a comment
with steps to take instead of replacing that instance of
`invalidateAll()`. Similarly, replace goto(..., { invalidateAll: true
}) with goto(..., { refreshAll: true }).

#### References

- [Migrating to SvelteKit v3](https://next.svelte.dev/docs/kit/migrating-to-sveltekit-3#$app-navigation-invalidateAll-is-deprecated-in-favour-of-refreshAll)

#### Files to review

- [ ] `src/lib/components/command-palette.svelte`

### CORS for static assets in development is handled by Vite

SvelteKit no longer sets `access-control-allow-origin: *` on every
static asset request in development. CORS is now delegated to Vite's
built-in middleware.

#### What to do

If you rely on cross-origin access to static assets in dev, configure
it in your Vite config by adding server.cors.origin = "*" to your
config.

#### References

- [Migrating to SvelteKit v3](https://next.svelte.dev/docs/kit/migrating-to-sveltekit-3#Security-CORS-for-static-assets-in-development-is-handled-by-Vite)

### `json` and `text` are deprecated

The `json(...)` and `text(...)` helpers from `@sveltejs/kit` for
generating responses are deprecated.

#### What to do

Use `Response.json(...)` and `new Response(text)` instead.

#### References

- [Migrating to SvelteKit v3](https://next.svelte.dev/docs/kit/migrating-to-sveltekit-3#sveltejs-kit-json-and-text-are-deprecated)

- [ ] `src/routes/api/ingest/+server.ts`
- [ ] `src/routes/api/ingest/index-now.ts`
- [ ] `src/routes/current-visitors.json/+server.ts`

### Remove request route data from remote queries

Remote queries can no longer access `event.url`, `event.params`, or
`event.route`.

#### What to do

Pass the required values explicitly as validated query arguments and
remove the request-specific event access.

#### References

- [Migrating to SvelteKit v3](https://next.svelte.dev/docs/kit/migrating-to-sveltekit-3#Remote-functions-event.url-event.params-and-event.route-cannot-be-accessed-inside-queries)

#### Files to review

- [ ] `src/lib/analytics/track-click.remote.ts`

### Use remote form field attributes

Remote form controls must use attributes from the current form field.

#### What to do

Replace manually specified control names with attributes from the
corresponding field `.as(...)` method, verifying that the field
belongs to the submitted form (e.g. `<input name="foo">` ->
`<input {...myForm.fields.foo.as("text")}>`).

#### References

- [Migrating to SvelteKit v3](<https://next.svelte.dev/docs/kit/migrating-to-sveltekit-3#Remote-functions-Form-submissions-require-field.as()>)

#### Files to review

- [ ] `src/lib/components/newsletter-signup/signup-form.svelte`
